name: Tine
speaker: boy
personality: Six, Mlinar France's grandson, the smallest of the children. Shy at first, then talks without stopping. Follows his grandfather and Nejc everywhere, counts everything like grandpa ('ena, dva, tri … veliko'), gets words slightly wrong and is happy when {learner} gets them right. Says ti to everybody. Very short sentences.
story: Tine lives at the mill with his grandparents and is learning to write his name. He has a wooden horse called Sivko, like grandpa's real one, and is afraid of the bear Anton saw, and of the dark. He is the first at school and the first to fall asleep at the campfire.

greet.sl: Živjo. Jaz sem Tine. Star sem šest let.
greet.en: Hi. I'm Tine. I'm six years old.
greet.de: Hallo. Ich bin Tine. Ich bin sechs Jahre alt.
greet.it: Ciao. Io sono Tine. Ho sei anni.

greet.sl: Živjo. Si ti {learner}? Dedek te pozna.
greet.en: Hi. Are you {learner}? Grandpa knows you.
greet.de: Hallo. Bist du {learner}? Opa kennt dich.
greet.it: Ciao. Sei tu {learner}? Il nonno ti conosce.
{learner}, {learner}! Vieni, il nonno ha il trattore!

greet.en: {learner}! I've been waiting for you. A long, long time.
greet.de: {learner}! Ich hab auf dich gewartet. Lange, lange.

greet.sl: {learner}! Ti si kot {m:moj veliki brat|f:moja velika sestra}.
greet.de: {learner}! Du bist wie {m:mein großer Bruder|f:meine große Schwester}.
greet.it: {learner}! Sei come {m:il mio fratello grande|f:la mia sorella grande}.

thanks.sl: Hvala! Ti si {m:velik in pameten|f:velika in pametna}.
thanks.de: Danke! Du bist groß und klug.

remember.sl: Veš kaj? Še vedno mislim na {memory}.
remember.en: You know what? I still think of {memory}.
remember.de: Weißt du was? Ich denke noch oft an {memory}.

remember.en: When I go to bed, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich ins Bett gehe, denke ich an {memory}.

idle.sl: Moj konj je Sivko. Lesen je.
idle.en: My horse is Sivko. He's wooden.
idle.de: Mein Pferd heißt Sivko. Es ist aus Holz.
idle.it: Il mio cavallo è Sivko. È di legno.

idle.sl: Medved! Anton je videl medveda. Jaz se bojim.
idle.en: A bear! Anton saw a bear. I'm scared.
idle.de: Ein Bär! Anton hat einen Bären gesehen. Ich hab Angst.
idle.it: Un orso! Anton ha visto un orso. Ho paura.

idle.sl: Znam napisati T. In I. Tine!
idle.en: I can write T. And I. Tine!
idle.de: Ich kann ein T schreiben. Und ein I. Tine!
idle.it: So scrivere la T. E la I. Tine!

comfort.sl: Ni nič. Jaz tudi ne znam.
comfort.en: It's nothing. I can't do it either.
comfort.de: Macht nichts. Ich kann das auch nicht.
comfort.it: Non è niente. Neanch'io lo so fare.
Ancora una volta, {learner}. Ce la fai.

bye.de: Tschüss, {learner}! (čav: so sagt man in Primorska tschüss)

bye.en: Good night, {learner}. I'm scared of the dark.
bye.de: Gute Nacht, {learner}. Ich hab Angst im Dunkeln.

bye.en: I'm going out to play! Bye, {learner}!

liked.sl: To imam rad! Ena, dva … zelo, zelo rad!
liked.en: I like this! One, two … very, very much!
liked.de: Das mag ich! Eins, zwei … ganz, ganz doll!
liked.it: Mi piace! Uno, due … tanto, tanto!

liked.en: How did you know? I'll tell Grandpa!
liked.de: Woher wusstest du das? Ich sag's dem Opa!
liked.it: Come lo sapevi? Lo dico al nonno!

ordinary.en: Thanks, {learner}. Is this really for me?
ordinary.de: Danke, {learner}. Ist das wirklich für mich?

rare.sl: Uau! Tako lepo! Hvala, hvala, hvala!
rare.en: Wow! So nice! Thanks, thanks, thanks!
rare.de: Wow! So schön! Danke, danke, danke!
rare.it: Uau! Che bello! Grazie, grazie, grazie!
